note: Planning values for restaurant and similar commercial buildings. Layer rows are material resistances. Assembly rows are whole-element coefficients. Climate-zone rows are IECC prescriptive limits for zone 5 and marine 4, all other, not a test of a specific building. SHGC is omitted where the cited source did not state it. Loading a user file adds ids that are not already present.

materials.name: Heavyweight concrete slab, 4 in
materials.typicalUse: Slab-on-grade structure under dining, kitchen, and back-of-house
materials.source: Energy Code Ace layer table, heavyweight undried aggregate concrete, 4 in, R-0.32 (layer CC14).
materials.notes: Layer resistance only. Heat loss from a slab-on-grade to the ground is an F-factor, not this R.

materials.name: Ceramic or quarry tile
materials.typicalUse: Kitchen, restroom, and servery finish
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, tile, R-0.05.
materials.notes: Finish layer only. Thickness was not stated. Add the slab row for the structure under the tile.

materials.name: Tile on a 4 in heavyweight slab
materials.typicalUse: Kitchen, dish room, and restroom floor
materials.source: Sum of tile R-0.05 and 4 in heavyweight undried concrete R-0.32.
materials.notes: Air films, grout, and soil are not included. Tile thickness was not stated, so the stored thickness is the slab only.

materials.name: Carpet with a fibrous pad
materials.typicalUse: Dining room finish
materials.source: Energy Code Ace layer CP01 and the Building Material R-Values table, carpet with fibrous pad, R-2.08.
materials.notes: Finish layer only. Thickness was not stated.

materials.name: Mass floor, R-10 continuous
materials.typicalUse: Floor over unconditioned space in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, mass floor, U-0.074.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-10 continuous insulation for that class. 1/U is not stored, because that reciprocal is not the listed R.

materials.name: Joist floor, R-30
materials.typicalUse: Framed floor over unconditioned space in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, joist or framing floor, U-0.033.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-30 for that class.

materials.name: Unheated slab, R-10 for 24 in
materials.typicalUse: Perimeter insulation under an unheated commercial slab in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.3, climate zone 5 and marine 4, unheated slab, R-10 for 24 in below.
materials.notes: Code minimum insulation R, not the heat loss of the whole slab. The same sample lists a maximum F-factor of 0.54 for that unheated slab.

materials.name: Walk-in floor panel
materials.typicalUse: Prefabricated walk-in cooler or freezer floor on a slab
materials.source: U.S. Cooler walk-in specification, exposed prefabricated floor panels, R-28 or greater.
materials.notes: Published minimum. Thickness was not stated for the floor. The same sheet says freezer floors may need subfloor heat.

materials.name: 8 in concrete masonry, uninsulated
materials.typicalUse: Uninsulated restaurant shell or existing masonry
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, concrete masonry unit, 8 in, R-1.11.
materials.notes: Uninsulated block. Grout, density, and interior finish are not included.

materials.name: 12 in concrete masonry, uninsulated
materials.typicalUse: Uninsulated masonry shell
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, concrete masonry unit, 12 in, R-1.28.
materials.notes: Uninsulated block. Grout, density, and interior finish are not included.

materials.name: Face brick, 4 in
materials.typicalUse: Dining-room or street-front veneer
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, face brick, 4 in, R-0.44.
materials.notes: One wythe only. Backup and insulation are separate.

materials.name: Common brick, 4 in
materials.typicalUse: Masonry wythe
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, common brick, 4 in, R-0.80.
materials.notes: One wythe only.

materials.name: Gypsum board, 1/2 in
materials.typicalUse: Interior finish on studs or furring
materials.source: Energy Code Ace layer GP01, gypsum board, 1/2 in, R-0.45.
materials.notes: Finish layer only. The same row lists density 50 lb/ft³.

materials.name: Metal-framed wall, R-13 + R-7.5 ci
materials.typicalUse: Insulated stud wall for a conditioned restaurant in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, metal framed, U-0.064.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-13 plus R-7.5 continuous insulation for metal-framed walls. Other climate zones differ.

materials.name: Metal building wall, R-13 + R-13 ci
materials.typicalUse: Insulated metal-building shell in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, metal building wall, U-0.052.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-13 plus R-13 continuous insulation for metal-building walls.

materials.name: Wood-framed wall, R-13 + R-3.8 ci or R-20
materials.typicalUse: Wood stud wall in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, wood framed and other, U-0.064.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-13 plus R-3.8 continuous insulation, or R-20, for that class.

materials.name: Mass wall, R-11.4 continuous
materials.typicalUse: Insulated masonry or concrete wall in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, mass wall, U-0.090.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-11.4 continuous insulation for above-grade mass walls.

materials.name: Walk-in cooler panel, 4 in XPS
materials.typicalUse: Prefabricated walk-in cooler wall
materials.source: U.S. Cooler walk-in specification, cooler walls and ceiling, 4 in extruded polystyrene, minimum R-28.8.
materials.notes: Manufacturer minimum, about R-7.2 per inch. Freezer panels on the same sheet are listed at R-32.

materials.name: Walk-in freezer panel, 4 in XPS
materials.typicalUse: Prefabricated walk-in freezer wall
materials.source: U.S. Cooler walk-in specification, freezer walls and ceiling, 4 in extruded polystyrene, minimum R-32.
materials.notes: Manufacturer minimum, about R-8 per inch.

materials.name: Acoustic ceiling tile, 1/2 in
materials.typicalUse: Dropped ceiling in dining, office, or corridor
materials.source: Energy Code Ace layer AC02, 1/2 in acoustic tile, R-1.26.
materials.notes: Tile only. The roof or the plenum above is a separate assembly.

materials.name: Walk-in cooler ceiling panel, 4 in XPS
materials.typicalUse: Prefabricated walk-in cooler ceiling
materials.source: U.S. Cooler walk-in specification, cooler walls and ceiling, 4 in extruded polystyrene, minimum R-28.8.
materials.notes: Same published minimum as the cooler wall panel.

materials.name: Walk-in freezer ceiling panel, 4 in XPS
materials.typicalUse: Prefabricated walk-in freezer ceiling
materials.source: U.S. Cooler walk-in specification, freezer walls and ceiling, 4 in extruded polystyrene, minimum R-32.
materials.notes: Same published minimum as the freezer wall panel.

materials.name: Roof, insulation entirely above deck, R-30 ci
materials.typicalUse: Flat roof over a conditioned restaurant in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, insulation entirely above deck, U-0.032.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-30 continuous insulation for that roof class.

materials.name: Metal building roof, R-19 + R-11 liner
materials.typicalUse: Metal-building roof in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, metal building roof, U-0.035.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-19 plus R-11 liner system.

materials.name: Attic roof, R-38
materials.typicalUse: Attic over a conditioned restaurant in a cold climate
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, attic and other, U-0.027.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor. The R-value table in the same sample lists R-38 for that class.

materials.name: Built-up roofing, 3/8 in
materials.typicalUse: Roof membrane layer
materials.source: Energy Code Ace layer BR01, built-up roofing, 3/8 in, R-0.33.
materials.notes: Membrane layer only. Insulation above the deck is a separate row.

materials.name: Single glazing in a metal frame
materials.typicalUse: Older storefront or uninsulated window
materials.source: Engineering Toolbox transmission-loss table, vertical single glazing in a metal frame, 5.8 W/(m²·K).
materials.notes: Whole-window coefficient from that table. SHGC was not stated. Glass thickness was not stated.

materials.name: Sealed double glazing, 20 mm gap
materials.typicalUse: Double-pane window without a stated low-E coating
materials.source: Engineering Toolbox transmission-loss table, vertical sealed double glazing, 20 mm between glasses, 3.0 W/(m²·K).
materials.notes: SHGC was not stated. Frame type was not stated for this row.

materials.name: Double glazing with a low-E coating
materials.typicalUse: Typical newer storefront or dining-room window
materials.source: Engineering Toolbox transmission-loss table, vertical sealed double glazing with a low-E coating, U-0.32 and 1.8 W/(m²·K).
materials.notes: SHGC was not stated. Confirm the product label before using a solar-gain load.

materials.name: Double glazing, low-E, heavy gas fill
materials.typicalUse: Higher-performance double-pane window
materials.source: Engineering Toolbox transmission-loss table, double glazing with a low-E coating and heavy gas fill, U-0.27 and 1.5 W/(m²·K).
materials.notes: SHGC was not stated.

materials.name: Uninsulated single-layer metal door
materials.typicalUse: Older service door or uninsulated hatch
materials.source: ASHRAE 90.1-2007 Section A7, Energy Code Ace Table 4.5.1, uninsulated single-layer metal swinging door, U-1.45.
materials.notes: That row also covers uninsulated access hatches and uninsulated smoke vents. Thickness was not stated.

materials.name: Uninsulated double-layer metal door
materials.typicalUse: Uninsulated hollow metal door
materials.source: ASHRAE 90.1-2007 Section A7, Energy Code Ace Table 4.5.1, uninsulated double-layer metal door, U-0.70.
materials.notes: Thickness was not stated.

materials.name: Insulated metal swinging door
materials.typicalUse: Typical commercial entry or kitchen door when the tested label is unknown
materials.source: ASHRAE 90.1-2007 Section A7, Energy Code Ace Table 4.5.1, insulated metal swinging door, U-0.50.
materials.notes: Default coefficient, including fire-rated doors in that row. A separate published table lists a 2 in insulated metal door at R-15, which is a different claim. Use the door label when you have one.

materials.name: Insulated metal door, 2 in, R-15
materials.typicalUse: High-R insulated metal door
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, insulated metal door, 2 in, R-15.
materials.notes: Much higher than the ASHRAE 90.1-2007 default U-0.50 for insulated metal swinging doors. Treat it as that table's product-style R, and prefer a tested label.

materials.name: Wood door, 1-3/4 in minimum
materials.typicalUse: Wood swinging door of at least 1-3/4 in nominal thickness
materials.source: ASHRAE 90.1-2007 Section A7, Energy Code Ace Table 4.5.1, wood door minimum nominal 1-3/4 in, U-0.50.
materials.notes: That row includes solid-core flush doors, hollow-core flush doors, and panel doors with a minimum panel thickness of 1-1/8 in.

materials.name: Solid-core wood door, 1-3/4 in
materials.typicalUse: Solid-core wood door
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, solid-core wood, 1-3/4 in, R-2.17.
materials.notes: Close to, but not the same as, the ASHRAE 90.1-2007 default U-0.50 for a 1-3/4 in wood door.

materials.name: Swinging opaque door, code maximum
materials.typicalUse: Opaque swinging door used to meet a cold-climate prescriptive limit
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5 and marine 4, all other, swinging door, U-0.37.
materials.notes: Code maximum U-factor, not a specific door. Thickness was not stated.

materials.name: Fiberglass batt, R-13
materials.typicalUse: Cavity insulation in a 3.5 in stud wall
materials.source: IECC commercial envelope sample names R-13 cavity insulation for the zone 5 metal-framed wall. A labeled R-13 batt is nominally 3.5 in.
materials.notes: Labeled batt R, not the whole-wall U-factor. The same sample lists that wall class at a maximum U-0.064 when R-13 is combined with R-7.5 continuous insulation.

materials.name: Foil-faced polyisocyanurate, 1 in
materials.typicalUse: Continuous roof or wall insulation
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, foil-faced polyisocyanurate, 1 in, R-7.2.
materials.notes: Labeled product R at 1 in. Aged R and mean temperature change it.

materials.name: Site-foamed polyurethane, 1 in
materials.typicalUse: Field-applied foam insulation
materials.source: Building Material R-Values table, polyurethane foam foamed on site, 1 in, R-6.25.
materials.notes: Labeled product R at 1 in.

materials.name: Walk-in cooler XPS, 1 in
materials.typicalUse: Extruded polystyrene used in a walk-in cooler panel
materials.source: U.S. Cooler walk-in specification, cooler extruded polystyrene, R-7.2 per inch.
materials.notes: The same sheet lists freezer XPS at about R-8 per inch. This row is the cooler grade.
